sampling_model.design: Independent Bernoulli assignment of a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade algorithm with \(P(Z=1)=e\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.units: An independent and identically distributed sample of participants \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\) whose conditional arm-cell vector \(\mu\) lies in the explicit observable compatibility set \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary randomized assignment \(Z\) in a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment. Control retains baseline placement; the treatment algorithm may retain or upgrade a participant's assigned tier and is prohibited from downgrading it. Thus \(D_z\) records assigned tier rather than unrestricted voluntary firm choice. The cross-world condition \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\) is researcher-imposed, maintained, and neither validated nor point-identified by the observed arm margins.
sampling_model.overlap: The assignment probability satisfies \(0<e<1\). The maintained observable positive-denominator and inference-stability restriction is \(\sum_{d=1}^{L}\ell_d\ge\kappa>0\); it is not attributed to a one-stratum positive-mass theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The primitive is the finite vector of empirical arm-state probabilities \(\widehat\mu_n\); no smoothing or learned nuisance is required.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1(iii) gives sharp closed-form bounds for the weighted aggregate local controlled direct effect under multilayer sample selection.

Accessible arXiv v6 Proposition 2 gives sharp conditional probability-of-causation bounds for the always-observed subgroup under conditional random assignment, positive mass, and monotone binary sample selection; journal proposition identity was not independently verified.
Theorem 2 gives a closed sharp interval for the fraction negatively affected using Fr\'echet bounds on observed treatment-arm marginals.

Proposition 5 and equations (7)--(8) give sharp Fr\'echet bounds for benefit across ordered outcome categories without outcome monotonicity, with tiered harm obtained by reversing the ordered-category comparison.
The directional delta method applies to Hadamard directionally differentiable maps, and valid resampling estimates the directional derivative rather than bootstrapping a nonlinear map naively.
A shrinking finite-difference evaluation consistently estimates the law of a directionally differentiable transform pointwise.
Calibrated projection delivers confidence intervals for projections of partially identified parameters with uniform asymptotic validity.
Aggregated conditional linear-program support values are regular under a margin condition and admit root-\(n\) Gaussian inference.

body.tldr: Random assignment identifies the two arm-specific tier--outcome margins but not which participants retain the same positive assigned tier or which such participants are harmed. Here the layers are selectively observed, protocol-assigned selection tiers, not categories of the outcome. The maintained restriction \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\) is researcher-imposed strong monotonicity for a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment: control retains baseline placement, whereas the treatment algorithm may retain or upgrade an assigned tier but cannot downgrade it. It is distinct from ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity and is neither validated nor point-identified from observed arm margins. Under this restriction, the entire feasible diagonal of the response-type table is a Cartesian box, and binary potential-outcome completion converts each diagonal coordinate into an independent hinge region for harm. This exact cross-world stayer--harm prism yields sharp \(O(L)\) endpoints for a ratio with unidentified numerator and denominator and an observable iff certificate for unavoidable harm; an exact nondegenerate two-layer response table attains \([8/25,10/11]\). Fixed-\(L\) pointwise numerical-delta calculations and confidence-set image projection are implementation devices inherited from general results, not research contributions.

project_justification.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already supplies sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds under multilayer selection. Their Assumption 2 imposes only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits both directions among positive layers, so it neither states nor supports ordered-layer monotonicity. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele provide the closest multi-tier harm comparison: their sharp bounds concern movement across tiers of ordered outcome categories. Binary harm results handle one observed stratum or fully observed arm marginals. No inspected result characterizes harm within latent same-layer stayers jointly with an unidentified sum of same-tier stayer masses under selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers.
project_justification.niche: In a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment, a researcher may maintain strong monotonicity because control retains baseline placement and the treatment assignment algorithm is prohibited from downgrading tiers. This cross-world restriction is stronger than ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity and is not learned from the observed arm margins; conditional on it, upper-triangular support makes residual response-type transport strict triangular.
project_justification.fill: Three identification theorems establish the diagonal box, the exact joint stayer--harm prism, and sharp \(O(L)\) endpoints for protocol-assigned tiers. The unavoidable-harm corollary and exact rational two-layer attainment witness make the identification result directly auditable. Generic numerical-delta and confidence-set image operations remain ordinary implementation prose.

body.related_work: Kroft, Mourifi\'e, and Vayalinkal study multilayer sample selection, and their Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds. Their Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity: treatment cannot turn positive selection into nonselection, but movements in both directions among positive layers remain admissible. It therefore provides no precedent or support for the ordered-layer condition \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\). That condition is imposed solely by this paper as a cross-world protocol restriction for a tier-upgrade experiment in which control retains baseline placement and the treatment assignment algorithm cannot downgrade an assigned tier. It is stronger than ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity, and observed arm margins neither validate nor point-identify it. The contribution conditional on that restriction is the exact cross-world binary stayer--harm prism and the closed-form contraction of a ratio whose harm numerator and same-tier-stayer denominator are both unidentified. No applicability claim is made for settings in which tiers arise from unrestricted voluntary firm choice. The accessible arXiv v6 of Possebom and Riva derives sharp probability-of-causation bounds in one always-observed binary-selection stratum under conditional random assignment, positive mass, and monotone sample selection. As an explicitly non-novel boundary check, when all positive-layer mass is concentrated at one layer \(d^{\star}\), the present interval is \([\max\{0,q_{0d^{\star}}-q_{1d^{\star}}\}/r_{d^{\star}},\ \min\{q_{0d^{\star}},c_{d^{\star}}-q_{1d^{\star}}\}/r_{d^{\star}}]\). For \(q_{0d^{\star}}>0\), this formula follows by outcome complementation and identified-mass rescaling of Possebom--Riva, accessible arXiv:2210.01938v6, Proposition 2, using the factor \(q_{0d^{\star}}/r_{d^{\star}}\); for \(q_{0d^{\star}}=0\), both endpoints are zero directly. This cited specialization is not a research result or solve target. The journal article text was inaccessible during verification, so no claim is made that its proposition numbering or displayed formula is identical to arXiv v6. The maintained observable restriction \(\sum_d\ell_d\ge\kappa\) is imposed as a positive-denominator and inference-stability condition and is not attributed to Possebom--Riva's one-stratum positive-mass condition. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele provide the closer multi-tier harm comparator. Their Proposition 5 and equations (7)--(8) give sharp Fr\'echet bounds for benefit across tiers of ordered outcome categories without outcome monotonicity, and their tiered-harm analysis reverses that outcome-category comparison. Those outcome tiers are not the selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers \(D_z\) studied here. Their result neither supplies the ordered-selection diagonal box nor subsumes the joint region for latent same-layer stayer and harm masses or the resulting unidentified-denominator ratio endpoints. Kallus derives sharp fraction-harmed bounds from observed treatment-arm outcome marginals; his binary coupling informs completion within a fixed diagonal tier, not upper-triangular tier transport. Fang and Santos provide directional-delta calculus, and Hong and Li provide the pointwise numerical-delta theorem. For fixed \(L\), using the latter is a direct application after verifying the ambient directional derivative and conditional multinomial bootstrap premises, including the relevant boundary tangent space; no new inference theorem is claimed. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye provide substantive projection inference for partially identified parameters, while mapping a covered observable confidence set through \(H_-\) and \(H_+\) on \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\) is only the known image-of-a-covered-set fallback. Khandamiryan and Semenova study regular inference for aggregated conditional linear programs; that work is adjacent to, but not a comparator target for, the fixed finite-cell identification claims here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The observable floor \(\sum_d\ell_d\ge\kappa\) is a maintained positive-denominator and inference-stability restriction, not a theorem inherited from a binary always-observed stratum. The researcher-imposed condition \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\) is a separate, load-bearing cross-world restriction on protocol-assigned tiers. Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits both directions among positive layers, so it provides no support for this ordered-layer restriction. The restriction is stronger than ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity, is not validated or point-identified from observed arm margins, and is not credible for unrestricted voluntary firm choice without an enforcing assignment protocol. Reciprocal transitions between positive tiers can couple diagonal coordinates and destroy the box. For fixed \(L\), pointwise numerical-delta inference follows directly from Hong--Li after the ambient endpoint map's directional derivative and the conditional multinomial bootstrap premises are verified at the observable law, including structural-zero tangent directions; this implementation step carries no novelty claim and does not imply uniform validity along local sequences crossing a tie. The image of a simultaneous confidence region over \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\) is a known definition-level fallback, and its containment is not a research result. No growing-\(L\), covariate-assisted, efficiency, uniform-inference, regime-comparison, or empirical reanalysis claim is part of this core.
body.honest_scope: The research contribution is identification conditional on researcher-imposed strong monotonicity of protocol-assigned selection tiers: the diagonal box, exact joint binary stayer--harm prism, sharp closed-form ratio contraction, and iff harm certificate. These tiers index selectively observed assignments rather than the ordered outcome categories in de Aguas--Krumscheid--Pensar--Biele. A credible motivating design is a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment in which control retains baseline placement and the treatment algorithm may retain or upgrade but cannot downgrade the assigned tier. The restriction is maintained rather than inferred: it is distinct from ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity and is neither validated nor point-identified by observed arm margins. Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Assumption 2 permits both directions among positive layers and supplies no precedent or support for the ordering. The exact \(L=2\) arm-cell and response-law tables certify a nondegenerate attainable instance with bounds \([8/25,10/11]\), and the network decoder is supporting. The observable \(\kappa\)-floor is maintained for a uniformly positive target denominator and inferential stability rather than claimed as a published implication. Confidence-set image containment is retained only inside the implementation definition as a known fallback. Fixed-\(L\) pointwise numerical-delta inference is a direct Hong--Li application once the ambient directional derivative and conditional multinomial bootstrap premises are verified, with no novelty or separate theorem claim. The one-positive-layer formula is only a non-novel boundary check: for \(q_{0d^{\star}}>0\), it is the outcome-complemented arXiv:2210.01938v6 Possebom--Riva Proposition 2 interval rescaled by \(q_{0d^{\star}}/r_{d^{\star}}\), and the zero-mass case is immediate. It is not a formal solve target or contribution; journal proposition identity was not independently verified.
